blocks.text: E-commerce Manager — Fashion Business / Retail Management

blocks.label: Career category
blocks.text: Business, Finance & Entrepreneurship
QUALIFICATION
B.FTech / B.Des Fashion
Fashion Business / Retail Management
CAREER LEVEL
Entry to senior career
Online store operations to digital commerce leadership

An E-commerce Manager oversees a business's online sales channels and digital shopping experience. In fashion and retail, this includes managing product listings, online collections, pricing, promotions, inventory availability, customer journeys, conversion rates, and sales performance.
The role connects merchandising, marketing, technology, logistics, customer service, and business analytics to help an online store attract customers and convert visits into profitable sales.
Typical responsibilities

items.text: Manage the online product catalogue, descriptions, images, sizes, and product attributes.
Coordinate product launches, seasonal collections, promotions, and online campaigns.
Monitor online revenue, conversion rate, average order value, returns, and customer behaviour.
Coordinate inventory availability, fulfilment, delivery, and returns with operational teams.
Improve website navigation, search, product discovery, and checkout experience.
Collaborate with digital marketing teams on customer acquisition and retention.
Analyse sales and traffic reports to identify opportunities and operational issues.
Coordinate with website developers, designers, marketplaces, and technology vendors.

blocks.text: This career suits students interested in fashion retail, online business, customer experience, digital marketing, commercial strategy, and data-driven decision-making.
B.Des / B.FTech — Fashion Business or Retail Management
Build retail, merchandising, business, and digital commerce foundations
E-commerce / Digital Merchandising Intern
Learn catalogue management, product listings, and online sales reporting
E-commerce Executive / Online Store Specialist
Manage store operations, campaigns, catalogue accuracy, and performance tracking
E-commerce Manager
Own online sales performance, customer experience, and channel operations
Head of E-commerce / Digital Commerce Director
Lead channel strategy, budgets, teams, growth, and digital commerce operations

Graduates typically start in executive, analyst, catalogue, or digital merchandising roles. The time required to become an E-commerce Manager depends on business size, role scope, performance, and prior experience.
Year 1 — Fashion retail and digital business foundations
Academic focus

items.text: Fashion products, textiles, and retail fundamentals.
Introduction to marketing, branding, and consumer behaviour.
Business communication and basic accounting.
Principles of online retail and digital commerce.
Basic statistics, spreadsheets, and presentation skills.

blocks.text: Practical skills

items.text: Understand how fashion products are presented online.
Compare the shopping journeys of different fashion websites.
Write clear product descriptions and organise product attributes.
Learn basic Excel formulas, tables, and charts.
Identify how pricing, images, size information, and reviews affect purchasing decisions.

blocks.label: Suggested mini-project
blocks.text: Audit a fashion e-commerce website and recommend improvements to product discovery, product information, and the shopping experience.
Year 2 — E-commerce operations and merchandising
Academic focus

items.text: E-commerce business models and online retail operations.
Digital merchandising and catalogue management.
Retail pricing, promotions, and inventory fundamentals.
Search engine optimisation and digital marketing basics.
Order fulfilment, delivery, returns, and customer service.

blocks.text: Practical skills

items.text: Create structured product listings with accurate attributes.
Prepare an online product catalogue and promotional calendar.
Track orders, returns, cancellations, and inventory availability.
Understand product page optimisation and on-site search.
Calculate basic conversion rates, average order value, and sales growth.

blocks.label: Suggested mini-project
blocks.text: Create a mock online fashion store catalogue and a monthly merchandising plan with product categories, promotional activities, and performance measures.
Year 3 — Analytics, growth, and customer experience
Academic focus

items.text: E-commerce strategy and performance management.
Web analytics and customer journey analysis.
Conversion rate optimisation and usability.
Digital advertising, customer acquisition, and retention.
Customer relationship management and loyalty programmes.
Marketplace management and omnichannel retail.

blocks.text: Practical skills

items.text: Analyse traffic sources, conversion rates, and sales trends.
Identify where users abandon the shopping journey.
Compare the performance of products and campaigns.
Create dashboards using Excel or Power BI.
Develop hypotheses for improving product pages, checkout, or promotions.
Understand customer acquisition cost and contribution margin at a basic level.

blocks.label: Suggested mini-project
blocks.text: Build a dashboard for a simulated fashion store and recommend three improvements based on traffic, conversion, sales, returns, and average order value.
Year 4 — Strategy, commercial performance, and industry readiness
If the programme is four years long, use this stage for advanced electives, internships, and a capstone project.
Focus areas

items.text: E-commerce channel strategy and revenue planning.
Digital merchandising and product assortment optimisation.
Campaign budgeting and profitability analysis.
Website performance, usability, and conversion optimisation.
Marketplace operations, fulfilment, and returns management.
Customer retention, loyalty, and repeat-purchase strategy.

blocks.label: Capstone project
blocks.text: Develop an e-commerce growth plan for a fashion brand. Include target customers, catalogue structure, customer journey, digital marketing plan, operating model, revenue assumptions, key performance indicators, and a measurement dashboard.
Industry preparation

items.text: Complete an internship with a fashion retailer, e-commerce business, digital agency, or online marketplace.
Prepare case studies showing how data informed your recommendations.
Practise presenting commercial results and prioritising improvements.
Understand how online sales depend on inventory, logistics, marketing, and customer service working together.

blocks.text: E-commerce operations
Catalogue management, product listings, promotions, inventory coordination, order fulfilment, returns, and marketplace operations.
Business and data analytics
Revenue analysis, conversion rate, average order value, customer acquisition cost, returns analysis, and profitability tracking.
Digital customer experience
Website navigation, product discovery, mobile shopping, checkout optimisation, usability, and customer journey analysis.
Digital marketing and merchandising
Search optimisation, campaign coordination, product placement, promotional planning, customer retention, and online brand presentation.
Leadership and coordination
Project management, prioritisation, cross-functional communication, vendor coordination, and commercial decision-making.

rows.text: Online store setup, catalogue management, orders, and promotions
Website traffic, customer journeys, conversions, and campaign analysis

Search visibility and organic traffic monitoring

blocks.label: Recommended starting combination
blocks.text: Excel, Shopify or WooCommerce, Google Analytics 4, and basic SEO. Add Power BI and paid advertising tools as you progress.
E-commerce Operations
Manage catalogue accuracy, orders, inventory, fulfilment, returns, and daily store operations.
Operations
Digital Merchandising
Optimise product selection, online displays, category pages, recommendations, and promotions.
Merchandising
E-commerce Growth and Marketing
Improve customer acquisition, campaign performance, conversion, and repeat purchases.
Growth
Marketplace Management
Manage fashion products and commercial performance across third-party online marketplaces.
Marketplaces
E-commerce Analytics and Optimisation
Use customer and sales data to improve website performance, product discovery, and profitability.
Analytics
Build projects that show both business understanding and the ability to improve online sales performance.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Fashion e-commerce store
Create a mock store with product categories, product descriptions, size information, pricing, and a clear shopping journey.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Working demo store or documented storefront prototype.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Online sales performance dashboard
Analyse simulated sales, traffic, conversion, average order value, returns, and product-level performance.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Excel or Power BI dashboard with recommendations.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Shopping experience audit
Evaluate a fashion website's product discovery, mobile usability, product pages, and checkout journey.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Audit report with prioritised improvement ideas.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: E-commerce growth plan
Develop a campaign and merchandising plan to improve sales, customer acquisition, or repeat purchases for a hypothetical fashion brand.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Strategy presentation with goals, budget assumptions, and KPIs.
Use simulated or authorised data, state your assumptions, and distinguish recommendations from measured results.
Look for internships during the second or third year, or during the programme's designated internship period.

items.text: E-commerce Intern

blocks.text: Organisations and industry segments to investigate

items.text: Fashion e-commerce marketplaces.
Apparel and lifestyle brands with online stores.
Omnichannel retailers with both physical and online operations.
E-commerce service providers and digital marketing agencies.
Direct-to-consumer fashion startups.

blocks.text: Businesses such as Myntra, AJIO, Nykaa Fashion, and Tata CLiQ are examples to research, alongside fashion brands operating their own online stores. These are not confirmed current vacancies; verify opportunities through official careers pages and college placement channels.
What to learn during an internship

items.text: How product catalogues are created and maintained.
How promotions and seasonal launches are coordinated.
How online sales, conversion, and returns are monitored.
How inventory and fulfilment affect customer satisfaction.
How marketing, merchandising, technology, and operations teams work together.

rows.text: Store setup, catalogue management, orders, and promotions
Traffic, conversions, funnels, and customer behaviour
SEO, paid campaigns, email marketing, and customer acquisition
Sales reporting, inventory analysis, and commercial KPIs
Usability, mobile shopping, product discovery, and checkout design
Excel, Power BI, forecasting, and performance reporting

blocks.text: Consider practical courses from recognised platform providers and established learning institutions. Check current availability and choose courses that lead to demonstrable projects rather than relying on certificates alone.
Further study can support progression into strategy, growth, or digital commerce leadership, but it is not required for every e-commerce role.

blocks.label: MBA in Marketing
blocks.text: Digital marketing, customer strategy, and commercial growth.

blocks.label: MBA in Retail Management
blocks.text: Omnichannel retail, merchandising, and retail operations.

blocks.label: MBA in Business Analytics
blocks.text: Data-driven decisions, forecasting, and performance management.

items.text: Postgraduate study in Digital Business or E-commerce: Online business models, digital operations, and platform strategy.
Specialised study in Supply Chain Management: Inventory, fulfilment, returns, and logistics coordination.

blocks.text: Choose a programme based on your desired career direction, admission requirements, cost, and practical industry exposure.

rows.text: E-commerce Intern, Catalogue Executive, E-commerce Assistant, Marketplace Executive
E-commerce Executive, Digital Merchandising Executive, E-commerce Analyst
E-commerce Manager, Online Store Manager, Marketplace Manager, E-commerce Growth Manager
Head of E-commerce, Head of Digital Commerce, Director of E-commerce, Omnichannel Retail Director

blocks.text: Titles and responsibilities vary by employer. In smaller businesses, an E-commerce Manager may handle the website, campaigns, catalogue, and operations; in larger organisations, these functions may be divided across specialist teams.

blocks.label: AI-assisted merchandising
blocks.text: Using AI tools to support product descriptions, catalogue organisation, and product recommendations with appropriate review.

blocks.label: Personalised shopping
blocks.text: Tailoring product discovery and offers to customer preferences and behaviour.

blocks.label: Conversion optimisation
blocks.text: Improving product pages, checkout, search, and mobile usability through evidence-based testing.

blocks.label: Omnichannel commerce
blocks.text: Connecting online shopping with store inventory, pickup, returns, and customer service.

blocks.label: Social commerce
blocks.text: Selling through social platforms, creators, and live shopping formats.

blocks.label: Sustainable e-commerce
blocks.text: Improving product information, packaging, delivery efficiency, and returns management.

blocks.label: Commerce analytics
blocks.text: Using data to understand profitability, customer retention, inventory performance, and growth opportunities.

Reset checklist
By graduation, a career-ready candidate should be able to demonstrate:

items.text: A strong understanding of fashion retail and online business operations.
The ability to manage or prototype a product catalogue and online store.
Knowledge of digital merchandising, inventory, promotions, and customer journeys.
Practical Excel skills and familiarity with web analytics.
The ability to interpret sales and conversion data and recommend improvements.
A portfolio containing an online store, dashboard, audit, or growth plan.
Communication and coordination skills across marketing, technology, and operations.

blocks.label: Recommended first target
blocks.text: Aim for an E-commerce Intern, E-commerce Executive, Catalogue Executive, Digital Merchandising Executive, or Marketplace Operations role. Build experience in online store operations and commercial analytics before progressing toward E-commerce Manager and digital commerce leadership.
